source.title: ExpTest: Loss-Curve Hypothesis Testing for Autonomous Learning-Rate Selection in Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material supplied; text appears complete and readable, though the arXiv version date shown is later than the supplied study year.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training-loss results for neural networks trained with SGD/SGD with momentum and an autonomous learning-rate controller. This is a conceptual test of V1's training-error outcome, but its reported main classification results are test accuracy and qualitative training-loss curves, not training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper tests ExpTest as a learning-rate controller; relevant reported outcomes include training-loss curves and statements about minimum or convergent training loss. Test accuracies, regression results, and cited results are not rows for these claim versions. It does not test random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, student-teacher local minima, shortcut/depth comparisons, initialization alternatives, or the batch-normalization claims.
record.test_reason: The study uses linearized training dynamics and stability arguments to develop ExpTest and evaluates its controller's performance. Its qualitative loss comparisons do not establish V1's near-zero training classification error. The CIFAR-10 learning-rate reference is an input-covariance estimate, explicitly not a strict classification stability bound; convergence above it does not test V5's stability-threshold or curvature dynamics. No other version's intervention is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors present ExpTest as an autonomous global learning-rate controller with competitive performance across tested tasks. They acknowledge that its linearized motivation becomes approximate outside that regime. Theorem 1 establishes conditional properties of the learning-rate schedule, not by itself convergence of the loss or zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: ExpTest is a loss-curve hypothesis-testing learning-rate controller paired with SGD or SGD with momentum; the paper does not implement the cited studies' interventions on width, depth, shortcuts, initialization, above-stability learning rates, or normalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CIFAR-10 trajectory depends on optimizer and initial learning rate; CIFAR-10 loss trajectories vary in smoothness with batch size, while the text reports similar converged loss values across batch sizes. The ExpTest ablations also show test-accuracy changes when linear testing or Lipschitz upper-bounding is removed.

fits_no_version.finding: ExpTest reaches the lowest comparative CIFAR-10 training loss and similar losses across tested batch sizes, without readable numerical endpoints or training classification errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An autonomous learning-rate controller can achieve competitive training-loss convergence across initial comparator learning rates and batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: At 10ηmax, CIFAR-10 SGD converges qualitatively while momentum SGD initially converges and then diverges; ηmax is a covariance-based starting estimate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convergence above a covariance-derived learning-rate estimate depends on the optimizer in this VGG-16 experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: The controller's ablation, ImageNet and BERT results measure held-out accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ExpTest provides competitive held-out performance without manual initial learning-rate selection in several tested tasks.

record.problems: Most pertinent CIFAR-10 training-loss outcomes are qualitative and shown in plots, with no reported training classification error values. The CIFAR-10 comparison uses a modified VGG-16 and 75 epochs; the ImageNet ResNet-50 result is a single run and uses a different batch size and label smoothing from the cited original result.
record.rows_left_out: Test-accuracy and non-classification task results that do not measure training classification error are included only where they contextualize a relevant V1 training result; cited external outcomes and figure-only values without textual numerical descriptions are not separate rows. No relevant rows for V2–V6 because those versions' specified interventions and outcomes were not tested.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU spurious minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention through identity shortcuts or the specified alternative recipes.
Initialization comparisons measuring training speed, signal propagation or trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized-network stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, or matched Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V1 limits_scope labels: unavailable training-error measurements are an untested outcome, not evidence limiting the claim. The catapult mechanism is invoked as motivation, without a direct experimental test.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error values, corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100, or a model-size comparison; the relevant classification evidence is qualitative training loss for CIFAR-10.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and width differences.
Plain versus residual shortcut depth comparisons, including the specified datasets.
Comparisons among initialization schemes and trainable depth.
Learning-rate behavior above stability limits and curvature/sharpness dynamics.
Batch normalization versus no normalization as a training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance intervention.

rows.subject: modified VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with ExpTest and momentum 0.9 on CIFAR-10; compared training-loss curves across initial learning-rate settings.
rows.baseline: SGD with momentum at a well-chosen learning rate: essentially the same training curve
rows.value: ExpTest with momentum achieves the minimum training loss in all conditions
rows.note: The text describes minimum training loss comparatively but provides no numeric training-loss endpoint or training classification error.
rows.check: Lowest loss among compared methods does not establish near-zero training classification error. This experiment uses Simple ExpTest; distinguish it from the later Standard ExpTest with Lipschitz recalibration. The five initial learning rates describe comparator settings, not five distinct ExpTest initializations.

rows.subject: modified VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD and momentum at varied initial learning rates on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: This is an explicit mixed trajectory statement, but no numerical training classification error is given.
rows.check: Initial convergence followed by divergence does not measure V1's training classification error. The rate 10ηmax exceeds a covariance-based estimate, not an established initial-network stability threshold; no curvature trajectory is reported for V5.

rows.subject: modified VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD at varied initial learning rates on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: Convergence is described qualitatively; no numerical training classification error is reported.
rows.check: Qualitative convergence does not establish near-zero training classification error. Exceeding the covariance-based learning-rate estimate also does not establish V5's above-stability recovery.

rows.subject: modified VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with standard ExpTest, including Lipschitz upper-bounding, and SGD with momentum 0.9.
rows.note: Test accuracy does not establish the training classification error named in V1; the paper says the standard variant produced consistent performance gains.
rows.check: This is an ablation comparison of the study's own controller, measured by best test accuracy. It should not be a claim-evidence row.

rows.subject: modified VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained using ExpTest with batch-size correction at three batch sizes.
rows.value: All three batch sizes converge to similar loss values; smaller batch sizes display noisier trajectories
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the three batch-size conditions; no separate numeric training-loss values or training classification error.
rows.check: Similar converged training losses across batch sizes do not establish near-zero training classification error. The batch-size-1024 run also receives 300 epochs versus 75 for the other conditions.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with ExpTest, SGD and momentum 0.9 on ImageNet.
rows.note: This is a test accuracy comparison, not training classification error; the authors also note differing batch size and label smoothing.
rows.check: ImageNet test accuracy does not measure V1's CIFAR training classification error or V3's depth-and-shortcut comparison. The baseline is a cited external result under a different recipe; this should not be a claim-evidence row.

rows.subject: BERT-base-uncased
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned with ExpTest, SGD and momentum 0.9 on SST-2.
rows.value: ExpTest: 92.39 ± 0.42 mean accuracy; best single-trial accuracy 92.89%
rows.note: Validation accuracy does not establish the training classification error named in V1.
rows.check: BERT fine-tuning validation accuracy measures neither the system nor the outcome specified by V1. SST-2's validation split is used for evaluation, not training. This should not be a claim-evidence row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 modified VGG-16 trained with ExpTest and SGD with momentum
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports qualitative convergence and lower training loss, but no training classification error values; the result supports only a narrower qualitative outcome (R1, R3, R5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 modified VGG-16 at 10ηmax with SGD or SGD with momentum
reader_labels.reason: SGD is described as convergent, while SGD with momentum converges initially and then diverges, showing optimizer-dependent behavior (R2, R3).
